title: Fewshot staging schematic — scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for an intermediate ‘staging’ layer in the prompt library. Goal is to prototype a small scaffolding that sits between raw templates and production–ready prompt bundles used by SDKs and eval harnesses.

Why a staging schematic?
- Too many micro-templates bouncing between people (hard to reproduce).
- Need an intermediate set of deterministic transforms (token-budgeting + slot normalization) to detect brittle fewshot combinations earlier.
- Want to catalogue failure fingerprints (shortened answers, hallucination spikes, abrupt role-drift) by template composition.

High-level hypothesis:
If we capture a small set of metadata and deterministic transforms around each fewshot example (role, signal_strength, token_length_est, fragile_tokens), we can run cheap combinatorial checks and flag likely failure cases before expensive model runs.

Minimal data model (staging view) — notes to self:
- id: human-friendly short id (e.g., fs-2025-augA)
- canonical_prompt: single-shot human-readable prompt
- template_fragments: ordered list of fragment ids (S0, A1, Q2) — used to recompose variations
- metadata: role_hint / persona / domain / expected_length_bucket (short/med/long)
- signals: token_est, rare_word_ratio, named_entity_count
- fragile_flags: ["sensitive_dates", "exact-match-required", "numeric-precision"]
- test_vector_refs: list of tiny unit cases (3–8) for quick smoke

(Keeping this simple — earlier versions tried to be a full schema; we only need a staging subset.)

Experiment matrix (micro-runs):
1) Controlled reorder test — swap fragment order and run 20 samples through 7b and 13b open models. Watch for role inversion.
2) Slot compression test — compress fewshot exemplars to minimal tokens using anchor extraction (keep core exemplars only). Measure top-1 answer deviation.
3) Rare-token amplification — inject a single rare token in exemplar to surface brittle tokenization effects.
4) Prompt-length ramp — run exemplar sets with synthetic context expansions to measure hallucination onset point by token budget.

Example fewshot staging entry (draft):
- id: fs-2025-augA
- canonical_prompt: "You are a concise coding assistant. Given a short description, produce a minimal, runnable Python function (<= 20 lines) and a one-sentence explanation."
- template_fragments: ["role-brush", "task-open", "example-1", "example-2"]
- metadata: persona=concise-assistant; domain=code; expected_length_bucket=short
- signals: token_est=120; rare_word_ratio=0.02; named_entity_count=0
- fragile_flags: ["exact-match-required"]
- test_vector_refs: ["tv-parse-edge-1", "tv-async-4", "tv-expr-bignum-2"]

Sample small unit case (tv-parse-edge-1):
- input: "Write a function parse_version(\"1.2.03\") -> tuple ints"
- expected: minimal function splitting by '.' and mapping int with zero-trim; edge-case: leading zeros preserved as integer values (strip leading zeros then int).

Failure fingerprints to capture (examples observed):
- Short-circuit answers: model returns a single line comment instead of function (role-drift).
- Token-hopping hallucination: extra behavior appears only when two rare tokens align in exemplars.
- Numeric precision collapse: floats get rounded unexpectedly when exemplar contains scientific notation.

Quick heuristics to flag staging entries before model evals:
- If rare_word_ratio > 0.08 and named_entity_count > 2 => high-risk brittle tokenization.
- If expected_length_bucket=short and token_est>250 => mis-tagged exemplar (fix slot reduction).
- If fragile_flags contains "exact-match-required" and template_fragments length > 4 => flag: too many context signals.

Planned run pipeline (cheap smoke):
- Pre-check transforms (normalization, date masking) -> extract signals -> apply heuristics -> run 20-step micro-run on small model -> produce failure fingerprints -> append to entry.

Local quick commands (notes):
- python tools/staging_run.py --entry fs-2025-augA --model gpt-13b-mini --n 20 --seed 42
- tools/export_staging_csv.sh fs-* > /tmp/staging-summary.csv

Open questions / TODOs:
- How opinionated should transforms be? (mask dates vs leave raw) — lean conservative: mask only when tests show hallucination delta > 15%.
- Integration point with prompt-lib: should staging entries be implicit in PRs (lint check) or a separate review step?
- UX: add an optional human review flag when fragile_flags present.
- Small experiment: run daggered fewshot order permutations (all permutations up to length 4) on a held-out model to see combinatorial explosion threshold.

Notes to self (chaotic):
- Margot suggested a simple CSV-first approach (easier to diff in PRs). Good idea for now.
- Samir is curious about tokenizer diagnostics to automate rare_word_ratio — ask infra for a small tokenizer-endpoint hook. (JIRA-INFR-4321)
- Keep test vectors tiny (no more than 6) so staging checks are <200ms walltime on small GPU.

References / links (work-in-progress):
- Confluence outline: CONFLUENCE-7245 (staging proposal)
- Prompt library PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-lib/pull/238

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Draft CSV schema, push a tiny example (fs-2025-augA, fs-2025-augB).
- Write tools/staging_run.py minimal runner (wraps the model CLI, returns fingerprints).
- Sync with Margot on whether to include a human_review boolean field.

If I get time: prototype a tiny web UI render for staging entries so non-ML folks can flip fragile flags and run the cheap checks.

End of scratchpad.

-- avery
